provisional_claims.summary: census() averaged living-plant vitality over all selected tiles (including bare ground) instead of over living plants only; FIELD_GUIDE says vitality averages describe living plants.

provisional_claims.summary: gardening.rectangle excluded the right-hand column (range(left,right)); rectangles must be inclusive of both corners
provisional_claims.reproduction: gardening.rectangle(world,0,0,3,2) returned 9 tiles instead of 12 (x=3 missing). Fixed to range(left,right+1).

provisional_claims.summary: census() diversity used log base 2; FIELD_GUIDE specifies Shannon entropy with natural logarithms.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Garden with two species in equal numbers: diversity reported 1.0 (log2) instead of ln 2 = 0.6931. Changed math.log2 to math.log.

provisional_claims.summary: gardening.brush 'circle' shape used the diamond (Manhattan) test so circle == diamond; now uses Euclidean dx²+dy² <= r²

provisional_claims.summary: Planting suitability/recommendations ignored shelter from structures (used base cell.shade although effective_shade was imported); FIELD_GUIDE says planting advice accounts for shelter from structures.

provisional_claims.summary: transplant discarded the plant's stress (destination stress set to 0) though WORKBENCH.md says transplant carries age and stress; now destination inherits source stress

provisional_claims.summary: recommendations(empty_only=False) still omitted occupied tiles; the flag was validated but ignored (docs: recommendations "normally" omit occupied ground).

provisional_claims.summary: forecast() omitted the final day when days is not a multiple of every; FIELD_GUIDE: "--days 10 --every 3 samples elapsed days 0, 3, 6, 9 and 10" (records the final day).
provisional_claims.reproduction: forecast(create(34,8,6),10,3) timeline days were [0,3,6,9]; now [0,3,6,9,10].

provisional_claims.summary: craft checked inventory against single-unit cost instead of cost*amount, letting resources go negative

provisional_claims.summary: search_notes date range excluded the end day (start <= day < end), so default search (end = today) hid today's notes; WORKBENCH says the date range is inclusive.

provisional_claims.summary: nursery_water only added one day of hydration; WORKBENCH.md: "Watering restores a three-day supply" — now sets hydration to 3

provisional_claims.reproduction: Seed batch with hydration 0 grown 1 day: age went up by 1 (could become 'ready' while dry). Now age unchanged, vitality -20.

provisional_claims.summary: search_notes tag filter matched substrings of tags (tag 'pond' matched 'ponds'); tag filtering should match whole normalized tags.

provisional_claims.summary: plant_out only deducted 4 nutrients for the last seedling of a batch; every planted seedling must use four nutrient points from its site

provisional_claims.summary: complete_task ignored done=False and always marked the task complete, so tasks could not be reopened (WORKBENCH: tasks can be marked complete, reopened or deleted).

provisional_claims.summary: Season calendar off by one: engine.season() used (day//12+1)%4 so day 0 was Highsummer instead of Dawn; fixed to (day//12)%4 (matches examples/first-garden.json journal "Highsummer settles" on day 12).

provisional_claims.summary: CLI errors exited with status 1; PORTABILITY.md documents CLI errors go to stderr with exit code 2.

provisional_claims.summary: History chart plotted x positions as if the first observation were day 0 and the span were len-1 (index-based), and labelled axis 'Day 0'..'Day n-1'; FIELD_GUIDE: history charts place observations at their actual dates. Now uses first/last recorded days.

provisional_claims.summary: Shade map layer showed base ground shade; FIELD_GUIDE says shade maps show the shelter plants experience, including structures — render_map now uses habitat.effective_shade
provisional_claims.reproduction: set_structure(w,5,5,'shade_cloth'); render_map(w,'shade') title for tile 6,6 showed base shade (e.g. 56) instead of +15 sheltered value. Fixed.

provisional_claims.summary: field_calibration.estimate computed least-squares spread/covariance from raw timestamps (sum t² − (sum t)²/n), catastrophic cancellation with real clock timestamps (e.g. Unix seconds) gave wrong slopes/estimates. Now uses origin-relative, mean-centred deviations.

provisional_claims.summary: Studio server publish() with --file autosave assigned the new garden before saving and then pushed that *new* garden onto the undo stack: a save failure (500) left the unsaved garden live, and undo after an autosaved edit restored the same edit instead of the prior garden.
provisional_claims.reproduction: make_server(world,0,'g.json'); POST /api/command water (0,0); POST /api/undo -> garden still has the watering. Also make save path unwritable: POST returns 500 but /api/world shows the edit. Now saves first, then records the previous garden and publishes.

provisional_claims.summary: Irrigation allocation was not maximal: augmenting-path search skipped residual (reverse) arcs, so earlier routing could never be rerouted and deliveries fell short of what supply and pipe capacities permit. Residual arcs are now traversable.
provisional_claims.reproduction: allocate([tank->a cap1, a->b cap1, tank->b cap1, a->x cap1],'tank',{'b':1,'x':1},10) delivered total 1 (b only); max is 2 (tank->a->x, tank->b). Now 2.

provisional_claims.summary: Server undo history kept the oldest 30 entries (undo_stack[:30]) instead of the most recent 30, so after 30+ edits new edits were dropped from undo; and a new edit after undo did not clear the redo stack (docs: a new edit after undo starts a new branch).
provisional_claims.reproduction: Make 31 edits, undo -> reverts edit #30's predecessor rather than the latest edit. Edit, undo, new edit: /api/world still reports redo 1 and redo re-applies the abandoned branch. Now undo_stack[-30:] and redo cleared on new edits.

provisional_claims.summary: Server revision check only rejected revisions lower than current and accepted booleans; DESIGN: a stale or noninteger revision returns 409. Now any revision != current, or non-int (incl. true/false), returns 409.
provisional_claims.reproduction: POST /api/command with revision current+5 or revision:true returned 200. Now 409.

provisional_claims.summary: POST /api/import always replaced the imported save's revision (checked `"world" in body`), but legacy imports without a revision must retain the imported save's revision; only imports supplying a revision get a fresh one.
provisional_claims.reproduction: POST /api/import {world:<save with revision 3>} (no revision) returned revision current+1. Now keeps 3; with "revision" supplied it becomes current+1.

provisional_claims.summary: commands.execute accepted commands with unexpected top-level keys (e.g. a misplaced 'revision' or typo'd 'arg') and silently ignored them despite the 'Command accepts only op and args' check; now rejects keys other than op/args
provisional_claims.reproduction: execute(w,{'op':'rename','args':{'title':'x'},'revision':3}) succeeded; {'op':'tend','arg':{...}} ran with no args. Now ValueError 'Command accepts only op and args'.

provisional_claims.summary: Undo/redo set the restored garden's revision to its stored revision + 1, which can equal/precede revisions already seen, instead of a fresh revision (docs: undo and redo restore prior contents as fresh revisions).
provisional_claims.reproduction: Edits to revision 3, POST /api/undo returned revision 3 (stored 2 + 1) — same as the pre-undo revision, so a stale tab at rev 3 could overwrite. Now revision = current + 1 (4).

provisional_claims.summary: Irrigation solve merged search states by aggregate census (rounded averages) instead of the full garden state, discarding distinct gardens with equal summaries and returning suboptimal schedules. State identity now uses the full world, offset and remaining water.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(6,5,4); outlets north(demand10,[[0,0]]), south(demand10,[[4,3]]), pipes cap 20, choices open north / open south, days 3, supply 20: solve score was 703, exhaustive replay best is 704. Now 704.

provisional_claims.summary: save_merge treated every record id as an inherited base identity (_logical_id ignored origin), so records independently created on both replicas with the same id were merged/conflicted instead of kept separate. New ids are now keyed by replica origin; inherited ids by base.
provisional_claims.reproduction: base=create(34,6,4).to_dict(); left adds note 'left note' (id 1), right adds note 'right note' (id 1); reconcile(..., left_origin='desk', right_origin='field') returned a conflict on /records/notes/["base",1]; now ready with both notes (ids 2 and 3).

provisional_claims.summary: courier.precedes iterated over the later clock's peers instead of the earlier dot's peers, so any event whose writer was absent from another event's context counted as superseded — concurrent edits from two writers vanished entirely from observations()
provisional_claims.reproduction: a=new_packet('a'); put(a,'r',{'text':'one'}); b=new_packet('b'); put(b,'r',{'text':'two'}); observations(merge(a,b)) returned [] — now one conflicted record with ['one','two'].

provisional_claims.summary: courier.observations case-folded values when collapsing concurrent edits, so 'Fern' vs 'fern' merged into one value and lost exact spelling; COURIER.md: text retains exact spelling and case — distinct values now compared exactly
provisional_claims.reproduction: put(a,'r',{'text':'Fern'}); put(b,'r',{'text':'fern'}); observations(merge(a,b)) showed a single unconflicted 'fern'; now ['Fern','fern'] conflicted.

provisional_claims.summary: courier: a simultaneous edit and deletion hid the observation (any concurrent $alive=False head won); COURIER.md says it stays visible until reviewed — now visible when any concurrent alive head is true
provisional_claims.reproduction: Shared base packet; writer a puts new text, writer b removes the record concurrently; observations(merge) returned []. Now returns the record with the edited text.

provisional_claims.summary: courier.acknowledged used max across devices, reporting progress seen by any device (and missing acks did not reduce it); docs: progress seen by every named active device, missing ack supplies no progress — now min with 0 default
provisional_claims.reproduction: acknowledged({'p':{'a':5},'q':{'a':2}},['p','q']) returned {'a':5} (should be 2); acknowledged({'p':{'a':5}},['p','q']) returned {'a':5} (should be 0).

provisional_claims.summary: courier.put stored caller-supplied field values by reference, so later mutation of the caller's list/dict silently changed the packet; COURIER.md: supplied field values remain owned by the caller — values are now deep-copied
provisional_claims.reproduction: tags=['x']; put(p,'r',{'tags':tags}); tags.append('y'); observations(p) showed ['x','y']; now ['x'].

provisional_claims.summary: Courier: merging a projected selection (or any packet) could delete observations it did not include. _covered() used the max context across ALL records and project() kept contexts of unselected records, so events of other records were treated as already superseded and dropped. Coverage is now per-record and project() keeps only selected records' contexts.
provisional_claims.reproduction: s=new_packet('desk'); put(s,'A',{'text':'a'}); put(s,'B',{'text':'b'}); f=copy of s as peer 'field'; p=project(checkpoint(s),['A']); observations(merge(f,p)) lost record B; now keeps A and B.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier merge only rejected reuse of a writer's event identity when the record name differed; the same (peer,counter) carrying a different field/value was silently accepted (left copy won). Now any differing content for the same event identity is rejected.
provisional_claims.reproduction: a=new_packet('desk'); put(a,'n',{'text':'x'}); b=new_packet('desk'); put(b,'n',{'text':'y'}); merge(a,b) returned a packet; now raises ValueError('A writer sequence was reused with different content').

provisional_claims.summary: Courier merge kept the left packet's counter even when the right packet carried newer events from the same writer, so continuing the merged writer's work reused event identities and overwrote existing observations. Merged counter now advances to the writer's merged clock.
provisional_claims.reproduction: a=new_packet('desk'); put(a,'n',{'text':'1'}); old=deepcopy(a); put(a,'m',{'text':'2'}); m=merge(old,a); put(m,'k',{'text':'3'}); observations(m) lost record 'm' (desk:3/4 overwritten). Now m['counter']==4 and all three records remain.

provisional_claims.summary: courier.merge kept the left packet's counter even when the right packet carried later events from the same writer, so continuing the merged packet reused existing event identities (overwrote an event and later merges raised 'writer sequence was reused'); counter now advances to the merged clock for the left writer
provisional_claims.reproduction: p1=new_packet('w'); put(p1,'A',{'text':'one'}); p2=deepcopy(p1); put(p2,'A',{'text':'two'}); m=merge(p1,p2); put(m,'A',{'text':'three'}) overwrote dot [w,3] (p2's event); merge(m,p2) raised ValueError. Now counter continues at 5 and merges succeed.

provisional_claims.summary: Workspace catalog upgrade from format 1 rebuilt the label index (REINDEX) before installing the format-2 normalizer, leaving index keys computed with the old casefold-only function; upgraded catalogs then failed to find receipts (even by exact label). Install the new key function first, then REINDEX.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create a format-1 catalog DB with label 'Field  Pond' and index built with casefold key; open WorkspaceCatalog(path): search('field pond'), search('Field  Pond') and fullwidth search all returned []. Now each returns the receipt.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier: new events recorded the writer's whole packet clock as their causal context, so after merging a projection (selected observations) a later edit silently superseded edits to *other* observations the writer never received. COURIER.md: sharing one observation does not imply the recipient has seen another observation's edits. Event context is now the per-record coverage (record_clock).
provisional_claims.reproduction: desk: put A a1, B b1; field=merge(new_packet('field'),desk); desk: put B b2, A a2; field=merge(field,project(desk,['A'])); put(field,'B',{'text':'bf'}); observations(merge(field,desk)) showed B ['bf'] (desk's unseen b2 lost). Now B ['b2','bf'] conflict for review. Randomized model check (3 peers, put/remove/merge/project/checkpoint) now matches reference causal semantics.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier checkpoint() stamped every record's context with the whole packet clock, claiming coverage of edits the packet never received (e.g. after merging a projection); merging the compact packet with the full source then discarded those unseen edits and resurrected superseded values. Checkpoint contexts now use each record's actual coverage (record_clock).
provisional_claims.reproduction: desk: put B b0; field=merge(new_packet('field'),desk); desk: put B b1, put A a1; field=merge(field,project(desk,['A'])); ck=checkpoint(field); observations(merge(ck,desk)) gave B ['b0'] (desk's newer b1 dropped). Now B ['b1'].

provisional_claims.summary: Rain barrels added six moisture every day, including clear days; GROWING.md ('Rain barrels collect water on rainy days') and the classic-1 release description ('add six moisture on rainy days') limit the bonus to days with rainfall
provisional_claims.reproduction: water_balance on a rain_barrel tile with rain=0 returned 53 vs 47 for a plain tile (barrel filled on a clear day). Now 47 on clear days and +6 only when rain > 0.

provisional_claims.summary: Ensemble summaries paired treatment trials with the wrong controls: pairs = zip(all complete controls, paired trials) so when a source was excluded (failed trial) the remaining trials were compared against another source's control. Now pairs each paired replicate with its own control.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Two sources A (small) and B; treatment event tends a tile only valid in B, so A's trial fails. Summary compared B's trial with A's control (first control). Now final_delta uses B's control.

provisional_claims.summary: Ensemble cache hits relabelled outcomes with the cached run's identity (replicate/treatment of whichever node computed it first), so two sources with equal saves collapsed onto one label and the other source lost its outcome. The outcome identity is now always the requested replicate/treatment; cache_origin keeps provenance.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create ensemble with sources {'a': save, 'b': same save}; work: b's control/treatment outcomes carried identity replicate 'a', summary dropped 'b' (paired_replicates ['a']). Now both listed.

provisional_claims.summary: EnsembleStore.report(revision) recomputed the result from the current node outcomes instead of returning the archived envelope, so published reports for earlier revisions changed after later edits/work. report now returns the stored published envelope unchanged.
provisional_claims.reproduction: examples/ensemble.json: create, work, r0=report(e); edit plan:water events to [] and work; report(e,0) now showed the new zero deltas instead of r0. Now report(e,0)==r0.

provisional_claims.summary: Ensemble publish only validated the node's previously recorded reads (empty for never-computed nodes), so a computation started before a concurrent edit was accepted with stale inputs. Publish now also checks the digests of the inputs the computation actually read against the current head.
provisional_claims.reproduction: t=store.prepare(e); store.edit(e,{'plan:water':{'events':[]}}); store.publish(t, store.compute(t)) returned True (node published with old plan for new revision). Now returns False and the node stays pending.

provisional_claims.summary: history replay checkpoint cache was keyed only on the last event (events[-1:]), so corrected/forked histories sharing a final event reused the original's cached garden — corrections had no effect
provisional_claims.reproduction: create; append note 'first', note 'second', edit_note 2; correct(branch,{first_event: {'op':'note','args':{'content':'FIRST fixed'}}}) returned notes still showing 'first' (cache hit on last event). Now key covers the full event prefix and the correction applies.

provisional_claims.summary: history replay resolved object references to the author's original local number (event bindings) instead of the logical object's current id, so after a correction renumbered objects, later edits hit the wrong/missing object; HISTORY.md: references keep identifying the objects their authors selected
provisional_claims.reproduction: append note 'first', note 'second', edit_note ident 2; correct removing the 'first' event -> branch conflicted 'No notes entry with id 2'. Now the edit follows the logical 'second' note (now id 1) and the branch is ready.

provisional_claims.summary: Staged studies promoted a stage as soon as ONE source had complete control+treatments, while other trials were still pending (decision depended on worker completion order; later results ignored). _advance_if_ready now waits until the stage is terminal (all trials complete or failed), then decides or records failure.
provisional_claims.reproduction: examples/study.json: create; work_once repeatedly. Stage 0 report was saved after only 'north' finished, cohort/common = ['north'], 'south' excluded while still ready. Now report waits and common = ['north','south'].

provisional_claims.summary: Later study stages restarted every promoted treatment from the previous stage's CONTROL checkpoint, discarding the treatment's earlier care and results. Each (replicate, treatment) job now continues from its own previous-stage checkpoint.
provisional_claims.reproduction: examples/study.json run to completion: stage-1 'Water' job's parent anchor had treatment 'control' and its samples were the control's; now parent treatment is 'Water' and samples continue the Water trial.

provisional_claims.summary: history.rebase used the parent branch's current head as the merge base instead of the fork's recorded base_revision, so the updated parent's new events looked 'removed' locally and were silently dropped from the rebased result
provisional_claims.reproduction: append note 'base'; fork child; child appends 'child note'; parent appends 'parent later'; rebase(child, parent) -> notes ['base','child note'] ('parent later' lost). Now ['base','parent later','child note'].

provisional_claims.summary: history.cherry_pick identified events by command content, so an independently authored identical action (e.g. both branches watering tile 0,0) was treated as 'shared' and rejected/deduplicated; HISTORY.md: independently authored actions remain distinct — identity is now the event id
provisional_claims.reproduction: fork; child appends tend water (0,0); parent independently appends the same command; cherry_pick(child, parent, [child_event]) raised HistoryConflict 'An already present event has different content'. Now both actions are kept (shared events by id are still included once).

provisional_claims.summary: Campaigns ignored their recorded ecological release: runtime.execution_version() always returned CURRENT_VERSION ('conservation-2'), so classic-1 campaigns (work and replay) ran with conservation rain-barrel rules. It now returns the campaign definition's recorded runtime id.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create a campaign with --version classic-1 on a garden with a rain_barrel tile and rainy days; branch results matched conservation-2 (barrel moisture capped) instead of classic +6. Now classic-1 semantics apply.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign publish accepted results from stale/foreign workers: the guard was `(generation = ? OR owner != ?)`, so a worker whose lease had been reclaimed (or any non-owner) could overwrite progress. Now requires generation = ? AND owner = ?; also the branch update and its checkpoint are written in one transaction (previously COMMIT between them could leave progress without a checkpoint).
provisional_claims.reproduction: c1=store.claim(id, lease_seconds=1); advance clock 2s; c2=store.claim(id); store.publish(c1, compute(c1)) returned True and overwrote c2's branch. Now False.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign compact deleted checkpoints that existing forks descend from: the protected (ordinal, offset) set of descendant origins was computed but never consulted, so provenance() of a child then failed ('Checkpoint is unavailable'). Protected checkpoints are now kept.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Run first-garden campaign (12 days, examples/treatments.json), child=fork(c,2,1), compact(c,5) then provenance(child) raised ValueError; now checkpoint (2,1) survives and provenance works.

provisional_claims.summary: History cherry-pick identified events by a digest of their command text, so an independently authored action with the same command (e.g. two separate 'water 0,0' events) was treated as already present and dropped, or raised a false 'different content' conflict. HISTORY.md: a shared action is included once; independently authored actions remain distinct. Pick identity is now the event id.
provisional_claims.reproduction: fork f1,f2 from a branch; append {'op':'tend','args':{'x':0,'y':0,'action':'water'}} to both; cherry_pick(f2,f1,[f2's event]) raised HistoryConflict 'An already present event has different content'. Now the picked branch has both waterings (f1 events + 1).

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign fork re-applied care already performed at the checkpoint: default continuation kept events with offset >= fork offset (event at the checkpoint offset was replayed at child offset 0). Docs: care at the checkpoint is already part of the starting garden; now only events after the fork offset are carried (offset < e <= offset+days).
provisional_claims.reproduction: examples/treatments.json 'Extra water' (offsets 1 and 4): fork(c, 2, 1) continuation events were [offset 0, offset 3] — tile watered twice for offset 1. Now only [offset 3].

provisional_claims.summary: History rebase only respected the target branch's order of shared events (loop over (target,) only), so contradictory authored orders of shared actions were silently resolved in the target's favour and the 'order-conflict' path was unreachable. HISTORY.md: incompatible action orders require review. Now both local and target orders are enforced.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Fork A,B; append note x to A and water y to B; A2=cherry_pick(B,A,[y]) -> [x,y]; B2=cherry_pick(A,B,[x]) -> [y,x]; rebase(A2,B2) silently produced [y,x]. Now raises HistoryConflict kind 'order-conflict'.

provisional_claims.summary: History correct() interpreted numeric IDs in a replacement command against the branch's final garden instead of the garden at that point in the history (HISTORY.md), so replacing an early event with e.g. edit_note of a note later deleted failed or bound to the wrong object.
provisional_claims.reproduction: append note A (id 1), delete_entry notes 1, note B; correct(branch,{delete_event:{'op':'edit_note','args':{'ident':1,'content':'A fixed'}}}) raised 'No live object has that local ID'. Now replays the corrected prefix and yields notes [(1,'A fixed'),(2,'B')].

provisional_claims.summary: history_exchange._common_bases returned only the first maximal common ancestor (maximal[:1]); after criss-cross reconciliations the merge base ignored the other shared contribution, so a later reversion of that contribution was silently undone. All maximal bases are now combined (recursive base)
provisional_claims.reproduction: announce history with notes n1,n2; desk edits note1 (D1), field edits note2 (F1); both reconcile (M1 by desk, M2 by field); desk reverts field's edit (correct remove), field reverts desk's edit; reconcile(D2,F2) gave notes ['n1','field edit'] (one reversion lost, depending on hash order). Now ['n1','n2'] consistently. Script: .scratch_c/hx_test.py

provisional_claims.summary: History exchange reconciliation used only the first of several maximal common ancestors (_common_bases returned maximal[:1]) in criss-cross histories, so depending on publication id order a later reversion was lost (the stale correction won). HISTORY_EXCHANGE.md: repeated rounds must retain later edits and reversions, including when both collaborators previously combined the same work. All maximal bases are now merged into the virtual base.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Genesis G with note 'orig' (event e). Desk corrects e->'corrected' (D1); field adds a task (F1). Both reconcile D1/F1 (M1 desk, M2 field). Field corrects e back to 'orig' on M2 (F2); desk waters on M1 (D2). reconcile(D2,F2) returned note 'corrected' in ~half of runs (random ids). Now always 'orig'.

provisional_claims.summary: Hush season penalised glowcaps like every other plant (comfort -2); GROWING.md: Hush slows most plants while glowcaps remain suited to the season — glowcaps are now exempt from the Hush penalty
provisional_claims.reproduction: Garden at day 40 (Hush), glowcap on a tile at its preferred moisture 72/shade 82, vitality 50: after step vitality rose only +3 (same penalty as moss). Now +5, while moss/fern/clover still take the -2 Hush penalty. Oracles (first-garden, lantern-hollow) still reproduce.

provisional_claims.summary: History exchange reconciliation used only one of several maximal common ancestors (_common_bases returned maximal[:1]), so after criss-cross merges (both collaborators reconciled the same work) a later reversion was silently undone depending on publication hash order. All maximal bases are now merged into the virtual base.
provisional_claims.reproduction: announce G; desk publishes note A (P1), field note B (P2); both reconcile P1,P2 (M1,M2); desk corrects M1 removing A and publishes P3; field appends note C on M2 (P4); reconcile(P3,P4) returned [B, A, C] in ~half of runs (A resurrected). Now always [B, C]. Script: .scratch_b/hx_test.py

provisional_claims.summary: Engine ignored per-species lifespan from the field guide (hard-coded age > 105 for all), so glowcaps (guide lifespan 75) lived 30 days too long; plants now return to the soil after SPECIES_GUIDE[species]['lifespan']
provisional_claims.reproduction: Plant a glowcap, set age 75 vitality 90, step: it survived to age 76 (guide says lifespan 75). Now it returns to the soil; moss/fern/clover still use 105. Example oracles still reproduce.

provisional_claims.summary: exchange.import_csv advanced the garden revision by two (trial.revision = world.revision+1 then += 1), unlike every other edit (one revision per successful edit, cf. tend_many/apply_blueprint). Removed the extra increment.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(34,6,4); import_csv(w, export_csv(w)); w.revision was 2, now 1.

provisional_claims.summary: engine.phase() (position within the garden year) used day % 47 although the year has 48 days (4 seasons × 12); day 47 wrapped to 0 a day early and phases drifted from calendar_day year_day. Now day % 48.
provisional_claims.reproduction: from mosslight.engine import phase; phase(47) returned 0 and phase(48) 1; calendar_day(47)['year_day']==48. Now phase(47)==47, phase(48)==0.

provisional_claims.summary: Harvest did not start a new growth period: it only subtracted 5 from age, so a mature plant (e.g. age 30, harvest age 8) could be harvested again immediately and repeatedly. WORKBENCH: harvesting takes vigor and starts a new growth period before the next harvest — age now resets to 0 (like seed collection).
provisional_claims.reproduction: moss at (0,0) age 30 vitality 90: harvest -> fiber 3, age 25; second harvest immediately succeeded. Now age 0 and the second harvest is rejected until the plant regrows.

provisional_claims.summary: Save validation accepted journals of up to 200 events although a garden retains only the last 100 journal events (README/GROWING); inconsistent saves with 101-200 events loaded and kept oversize journals. Limit now 100, matching the other documented collection limits.
provisional_claims.reproduction: d=create(34,8,6).to_dict(); d['journal']=[{'day':0,'text':'x'}]*150; World.from_dict(d) succeeded (journal length 150). Now raises 'Invalid journal'.

provisional_claims.summary: Nursery batches stopped gaining vigor on hydrated days once 'ready' (+3 only while 'growing'); WORKBENCH.md: a batch needs watering even after it is ready and hydrated days improve its vigor — ready batches now gain vigor on watered days too (capped at 100)
provisional_claims.reproduction: start_seeds clover; step daily keeping it watered: vitality 63, 66 (ready) then stayed 66 on later hydrated days. Now 69, 72, ... while dry days still weaken by 20.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier recover() did not give a clear error for damaged slips: a non-string slip raised AttributeError, and slips with extra trailing characters were silently accepted (zlib ignored trailing data). recover now validates input type and requires a complete stream with no unused data, raising ValueError('The recovery slip is incomplete or damaged').
provisional_claims.reproduction: s=receipt('Fern unfurled'); recover(None) -> AttributeError; recover(s+'~') -> returned text without error. Now both raise the documented ValueError; valid slips still round-trip exactly (incl. Unicode, 2000 chars).

provisional_claims.summary: World.index accepted booleans as tile coordinates (isinstance check), so JSON commands like {"op":"tend","args":{"x":true,"y":0,...}} silently tended tile (1,0) instead of being rejected; all other validators treat booleans as non-integers. Coordinates now require exact ints.
provisional_claims.reproduction: execute(create(34,8,6),{'op':'tend','args':{'x':True,'y':0,'action':'water'}}) succeeded and watered tile 1,0. Now raises 'Coordinates must be integers'. Oracles (first-garden, lantern-hollow replay) still reproduce.
